title: A proper birational morphism to a normal integral curve is an isomorphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ and $E$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] separated schemes of finite type over $k$, each of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; thus both are curves over $k$ in the sense of [def-pc-curve]. Let $p:E\to C$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant $k$-morphism inducing an isomorphism of function fields $k(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(E)$. If every local ring of $C$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then $p$ is an isomorphism. No normality of $E$ and no perfection assumption on $k$ are required.
